chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his slave girl who used to go and come, and he had isolated himself from her and there did not happen to be anything from him to her. What do you say regarding the child? He (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that this should not be sold, O Saeed!'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Does he accuse her?' So I said, 'As for an apparent accusation, no.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So, does his family accuse her?' So I said, 'As for something apparent, no.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So how can you have the leeway that the child would not be necessitated on you?'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child born to a slave girl when the master is unsure if he is the father?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia legal principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) in paternity, where the master's uncertainty does not negate the child's status unless there is clear evidence of separation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the burden of proof lies on the one claiming disownment, while Imam al-Rida (AS) further clarifies that familial suspicion alone is insufficient to break the link of nasab. This ruling underscores the protection of the child's rights and social standing within the household structure.
